chunks: Muhammad ibn Umar al-Hafiz narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Abdullah al-Tamimi narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My Master Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha narrated to me, from his father Musa ibn Ja'far, from his father Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn, from Fatima bint Rasul Allah (peace be upon him and his family)
That the Prophet (peace be upon him) said to Ali (peace be upon him): 'Whoever I am his Wali (Master/Guardian), Ali is his Wali. And whoever I am his Imam (Leader), Ali is his Imam.'

key_terms.إِمَامٌ: Leader, guide, or one who leads in prayer and governance
key_terms.فَاطِمَةُ بِنْتُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: Fatima, the daughter of the Prophet, used here to specify the lineage of the narration
key_terms.وَلِيٌّ: Master, guardian, or one having authority

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Prophet's statement regarding Ali being the Wali and Imam of believers?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, presents a variant chain linking the Prophet directly to Fatima (bint Rasul Allah), emphasizing the familial and spiritual continuity of Imamate. It reinforces the Shia doctrine of *Nass* (designation) by equating the Prophet’s authority (*Wali* and *Imam*) with that of Ali, establishing him as the immediate successor in both religious and temporal leadership.
